READ THIS DOCUMENT COMPLETELY BEFORE STARTING.
Your assigned problem statement will be provided by the organizers. You are expected to interpret the
requirement, make sensible product decisions, build a functional MVP, deploy it, and demonstrate it clearly.
Page 1
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
01 — Participant Instructions
This section applies to every participant, regardless of which problem statement you receive.
Objective
Build a simple but polished website based on your assigned problem statement. The challenge is intentionally
designed so that an MVP can be completed within approximately 5–6 hours using modern development tools,
including AI-assisted or vibe-coding workflows.
Time Limit
Total build time: 5–6 hours. Plan your time carefully. A smaller, complete, deployed product is more useful than
an unfinished website containing too many features.
Technology Rules
l You may use any suitable technology, framework, library, or no-code/low-code/vibe-coding platform.
l React, Next.js, Vite, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Tailwind, Bootstrap, or similar technologies are acceptable.
l AI tools are allowed. You may use AI assistants, website generators, code generators, or vibe-coding
platforms.
l A real backend is not compulsory unless you independently choose to build one. Mock data and local/static
data are acceptable.
l Do not spend most of the challenge implementing unnecessary backend infrastructure. Focus on the product
experience.
Design Expectations
l The website must be responsive and usable on desktop and mobile.
l Use a clear visual hierarchy, readable typography, consistent spacing, and sensible navigation.
l Use Git Club / CHARUSAT context where appropriate, but do not copy an existing website design.
l Avoid a completely generic AI-generated template. Your own design decisions should be visible.
l All visible text, labels, buttons, dates, and navigation should be checked for spelling and consistency.
l Use realistic sample data instead of repeatedly using placeholder text such as 'Lorem ipsum'.
Functionality Expectations
l Important buttons should do something meaningful.
l Navigation should work.
l Search, filters, tabs, forms, cards, modals, or other interactions mentioned in your problem statement should
function at least at MVP level.
l If a feature requires a backend but you did not implement one, simulate the interaction cleanly rather than
leaving a broken button.
What 'Complete' Means
A complete submission is not necessarily a large application. It is a focused MVP that solves the
assigned problem, works through its main user journey, looks professional, and is accessible
through a live URL.
Page 2
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
02 — Submission Instructions
You must submit exactly the following two things.
A. Live Working Website

another reliable hosting platform.
Submit the publicly accessible live URL.
Open the URL in an incognito/private browser before submitting and verify that it works without your local
development environment.
Do not submit only localhost links such as http://localhost:3000.
The evaluator should be able to explore the main features without needing your local machine.
B. 5–6 Minute Video on Google Drive
Record a short screen-recording demonstrating your final website. Upload this video to Google Drive and submit
the shareable link.

ID_Name_phone number

0:00–0:30
0:30–1:30
1:30–4:30
4:30–5:30
Introduce yourself and state the problem statement you were assigned.
Explain the problem and your approach / product idea.
Live demonstration of the main website flow and important features.
Show responsive behaviour, key design decisions, and any notable implementation.
5:30–6:00
Briefly mention what you would improve with more time.
Google Drive Sharing

l Set the Google Drive sharing permission so that the evaluator can view the video.
l Test the link from a different browser/account before submission.

l Live website URL opens successfully.
l Website works outside your local machine.
l Main user journey is functional.
l Website is reasonably responsive.
Page 3
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
l Video is approximately 5–6 minutes.
l Video is uploaded to Google Drive.
l Video filename follows ID_Name_phone number exactly.
l Google Drive link is accessible to evaluators.
l No broken links, obvious placeholder text, or unfinished sections.
Page 4
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
03 — Evaluation Criteria
The following criteria will be considered while reviewing submissions. The organizers may adjust the relative
emphasis depending on the assigned problem.
Area
What is looked for
Problem Understanding
Functionality
Does the website actually address the assigned requirement?
Do the important interactions and user journeys work?
UI / UX
Product Thinking
Is the interface clear, consistent, responsive, and easy to use?
Did the participant make sensible decisions beyond merely following the minimum list?
Visual Quality
Completeness
Typography, spacing, hierarchy, component consistency, imagery, and overall polish.
Is the MVP finished and deployed rather than being a collection of unfinished screens?
Demonstration
Does the video clearly communicate the working product and important decisions?
Important: More features do not automatically mean a better submission. Prioritize a coherent,
functional experience.
Page 5
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
Problem Statement 1 — Git Club Event Hub
Centralized Events & Activities Platform
The Problem
Git Club conducts workshops, competitions, hackathons, community activities, and other events. Information can
become scattered across Instagram, WhatsApp, registration forms, and individual announcements. Build a
central Event Hub where a student can discover what is happening, understand an event quickly, and access its
registration/details.
Your Goal
Create a clean, reusable event discovery website that Git Club could realistically continue using for
future events.
Minimum Required Features
l Git Club-branded navigation/header.
l Upcoming Events section with visually distinct event cards.
l Each event card should show event name, date, time, venue, event type, short description, and a clear action.
l Event detail view/page containing fuller information and a registration button.
l Past Events section.
l Search or filtering by event category.
l Responsive layout for mobile and desktop.
l Use realistic sample Git Club events rather than generic placeholder content.
Optional / Bonus Features
l Countdown to the next event.
l Add-to-calendar interaction.
l Featured event section.
l Category chips such as Workshop, Competition, Hackathon, Community, and Social.
l Past event statistics such as participants or editions.
Suggested User Journey
Home fi Browse upcoming events fi Filter/search fi Open an event fi Read details fi Registration
CTA
Product Thinking Prompt
Design the experience so that a first-year student who has never interacted with Git Club can understand what
the club is doing within a few seconds.
Implementation Guidance
Keep the scope realistic for the 5–6 hour window. You may use mock data. If a feature is not essential to the
main journey, treat it as bonus work rather than allowing it to delay deployment of the core website.
Page 6
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
Problem Statement 2 — Git Club Member
Directory
Discover the People Behind the Community
The Problem
A growing technical club can have students from different years, branches, teams, and technical interests. New
members may not know whom to approach for web development, AI/ML, design, event management, or other
domains. Build a Member Directory that makes the community easier to discover.
Your Goal
Create a professional people directory that could eventually become Git Club's internal community
showcase.
Minimum Required Features
l Member/team cards with profile photo, name, year, branch, role or interest, and social/profile links.
l Search members by name.
l Filters for at least year and role/domain.
l Individual member profile or expanded profile view.
l Separate leadership/core-team presentation.
l Responsive grid/list layout.
l Use realistic sample member data.
Optional / Bonus Features
l Skill or technology tags.
l People-you-might-want-to-connect-with section based on shared interests.
l Availability or 'Ask me about...' style information.
l Alphabetical sorting.
l Simple profile statistics.
Suggested User Journey
Directory fi Search/filter fi Select a person fi View profile fi Open GitHub/LinkedIn
Product Thinking Prompt
Avoid making this just a wall of profile cards. Think about how a student would actually use the directory to find
the right person.
Implementation Guidance
Keep the scope realistic for the 5–6 hour window. You may use mock data. If a feature is not essential to the
main journey, treat it as bonus work rather than allowing it to delay deployment of the core website.
Page 7
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
Problem Statement 3 — Git Club Project
Showcase
A Portfolio of What the Community Builds
The Problem
Git Club members create websites, apps, AI/ML systems, hardware projects, automation solutions, and other
technical work. These projects are often scattered across personal repositories and social media. Build a central
showcase that lets anyone explore the work produced by the community.
Your Goal
Create a polished project gallery that can grow into a long-term portfolio of Git Club projects.
Minimum Required Features
l Project cards with project name, thumbnail, short description, team members, and technologies.
l Project categories such as Web Development, AI/ML, App Development, IoT, Design, or other relevant
domains.
l Search and/or category filtering.
l GitHub repository button.
l Live demo button where applicable.
l Project detail page or modal with a deeper explanation.
l Featured projects section.
l Responsive design.
Optional / Bonus Features
l Technology-based filters.
l Project status such as Active, Completed, or In Development.
l Project detail structure: Problem fi Solution fi Tech Stack fi Screenshots fi Team fi Links.
l Featured/project-of-the-month area.
l Simple sorting by newest, featured, or category.
Suggested User Journey
Explore projects fi Filter/search fi Open project fi Understand problem & solution fi Visit
repository/demo
Product Thinking Prompt
The website should make even a visitor who does not know the project team understand what was built and why
it matters.
Implementation Guidance
Keep the scope realistic for the 5–6 hour window. You may use mock data. If a feature is not essential to the
main journey, treat it as bonus work rather than allowing it to delay deployment of the core website.
Page 8
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
Problem Statement 4 — Git Club Challenge
Arena
Learn by Building
The Problem
Technical clubs regularly run coding, design, web, and creative challenges. Participants need a central place to
discover challenges, understand requirements, track progress, and see their position in the community. Build a
mini challenge platform.
Your Goal
Create an MVP that feels like a real challenge/learning platform, even if the data and submissions are
simulated.
Minimum Required Features
l Challenge listing page.
l Challenge cards showing title, category, difficulty, deadline, and points.
l Challenge detail page with problem description, requirements, rules, and submission action.
l Submission interface or simulated submission flow.
l Participant leaderboard.
l Basic participant progress/status.
l Clear distinction between active, upcoming, and completed challenges.
l Responsive design.
Optional / Bonus Features
l XP and badge system.
l Streak counter.
l Animated leaderboard.
l Progress dashboard.
l Difficulty levels such as Easy, Medium, Hard.
l Mock submission status such as Not Started, In Progress, Submitted, or Completed.
Suggested User Journey
Challenge Arena fi Browse challenge fi Open details fi Start/submit fi See status fi View
leaderboard
Product Thinking Prompt
Make it feel like a product rather than a collection of pages. The participant should always know what they can
do next.
Implementation Guidance
Keep the scope realistic for the 5–6 hour window. You may use mock data. If a feature is not essential to the
main journey, treat it as bonus work rather than allowing it to delay deployment of the core website.
Page 9
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
Problem Statement 5 — Git Club Command
Center
The Club's Internal Dashboard
The Problem
Running a student technical club involves many moving parts: events, members, projects, announcements,
registrations, and ongoing activities. Build a Command Center that gives the club team a single high-level view
of its activities.
Your Goal
Create a dashboard that a future Git Club committee could realistically evolve into an internal
management tool.
Minimum Required Features
l Dashboard overview with key metrics such as members, upcoming events, active projects, and participants.
l Upcoming event summary.
l Member/team summary.
l Project/activity summary.
l Recent announcements or activity feed.
l Quick action buttons such as Create Event, Add Member, Add Project, or Publish Announcement.
l At least one meaningful chart or visual data representation.
l Responsive dashboard layout.
Optional / Bonus Features
l Event participation chart.
l Project status distribution.
l Recent registrations/activity.
l Date range or category filters.
l Dark/light theme.
l Mock notification center.
l Role-aware dashboard concept such as Admin, Event Lead, or Member.
Suggested User Journey
Dashboard fi Understand current status fi Inspect events/projects/members fi Take a quick action
Product Thinking Prompt
Prioritize information hierarchy. The dashboard should answer: What is happening? What needs attention?
What can I do next?
Implementation Guidance
Keep the scope realistic for the 5–6 hour window. You may use mock data. If a feature is not essential to the
main journey, treat it as bonus work rather than allowing it to delay deployment of the core website.
Page 10
Git Club CHARUSAT — Website Challenge
04 — Final Submission Reminder
Before you submit, verify every item below.
Website
l The live URL works.
l The website loads without local files or localhost.
l Main navigation works.
l Important interactions work.
l The website is responsive.
l No obvious broken images, buttons, routes, or placeholder content remain.
Video
l Duration is approximately 5–6 minutes.
l The video clearly demonstrates the working website.
l The video is uploaded to Google Drive.
l The Google Drive permission allows evaluators to view it.
l The filename is exactly in the required format: ID_Name_phone number.
l Example: 24CS084_Om_Rashiya_9876543210
Submission
1. Live Website
2. Demo Video
Paste your publicly accessible deployed website URL.
Paste the Google Drive shareable link to your 5–6 minute video.
3. Video Filename
Final Advice
ID_Name_phone number — compulsory format.
Start with the core user journey. Build the minimum required features first. Make the interface
polished. Test everything. Deploy before the final minutes. Then record a clear demonstration.
GIT CLUB • CHARUSAT
Build. Collaborate. Ship.

  // Technical Network Visualization Canvas Interactive Script
  (function initNetworkGraph() {
    const canvas = document.getElementById('gitNetworkCanvas');
    if (!canvas) return;
    const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
    let width, height;
    let nodes = [];
    const colors = ['#a9cfb9', '#ffb59e', '#e1c477']; // Sage, Coral, Gold

    function resize() {
      width = canvas.parentElement.clientWidth;
      height = canvas.parentElement.clientHeight;
      canvas.width = width * window.devicePixelRatio;
      canvas.height = height * window.devicePixelRatio;
      ctx.scale(window.devicePixelRatio, window.devicePixelRatio);
    }

    function initNodes() {
      nodes = [];
      const nodeCount = Math.floor(Math.min(width / 24, 38));
      for (let i = 0; i < nodeCount; i++) {
        nodes.push({
          x: Math.random() * width,
          y: Math.random() * height,
          vx: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.45,
          vy: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.45,
          radius: Math.random() * 2.2 + 1.8,
          color: colors[Math.floor(Math.random() * colors.length)],
          pulse: Math.random() * Math.PI
        });
      }
    }

    function draw() {
      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);

      // Draw subtle connections
      for (let i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {
        for (let j = i + 1; j < nodes.length; j++) {
          const dx = nodes[i].x - nodes[j].x;
          const dy = nodes[i].y - nodes[j].y;
          const dist = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);

          if (dist < 90) {
            ctx.beginPath();
            ctx.moveTo(nodes[i].x, nodes[i].y);
            ctx.lineTo(nodes[j].x, nodes[j].y);
            const alpha = (1 - dist / 90) * 0.22;
            ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(169, 207, 185, ${alpha})`;
            ctx.lineWidth = 1;
            ctx.stroke();
          }
        }
      }

      // Draw nodes
      for (let i = 0; i < nodes.length; i++) {
        const n = nodes[i];
        n.x += n.vx;
        n.y += n.vy;
        n.pulse += 0.03;

        if (n.x < 0 || n.x > width) n.vx *= -1;
        if (n.y < 0 || n.y > height) n.vy *= -1;

        ctx.beginPath();
        const animatedRadius = n.radius + Math.sin(n.pulse) * 0.6;
        ctx.arc(n.x, n.y, Math.max(1, animatedRadius), 0, Math.PI * 2);
        ctx.fillStyle = n.color;
        ctx.fill();
      }

      requestAnimationFrame(draw);
    }

    window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
      resize();
      initNodes();
    });

    resize();
    initNodes();
    requestAnimationFrame(draw);
  })();
